sections.overview: The Common Tern is a migratory seabird that breeds across much of the Northern Hemisphere.
sections.identification: It is a slender tern with long pointed wings, a forked tail and, in breeding plumage, a dark cap and red bill with a dark tip.
sections.habitat: It nests on open shores, islands and inland gravel or sand sites, often in colonies.
sections.diet: It catches small fish by hovering or diving down to the water; it also takes some aquatic invertebrates.
sections.behavior: It is a strong migrant and often gathers in groups when feeding or nesting.
sections.reproduction: It lays its eggs in a shallow ground scrape, and both members of the pair take part in caring for the nest.
sections.ecology: The Arctic Tern (Sterna paradisaea) is a close relative and more oceanic; it breeds at high latitudes and migrates to Antarctic waters. See its profile.
sections.conservation: BirdLife currently lists the Common Tern globally as Least Concern, while its population trend is reported as unknown.
